messages:
Marta: Pushed restream-cust LoRA merge to staging, ran a quick bakeoff. Seeing a small but consistent degradation on dialogue turn-taking for the int4 path. Can someone sanity-check?

Vikram: On it. Which eval set did you run? quickpack or longform?

Marta: quickpack v2 (1000 dialogs, weighted for negation/clarity). Baseline float32 vs merged-int4. Metric: turn-coherence dropped ~3.2% P@1, and some hallucination BLEU-ish artifacts.

Olivia: Can you drop the eval snippet and the exact model refs? put the merged artifact id and quant params.

Marta: Sure — artifact: restream-cust-lora:v3-merge-2026-03-19, quant: 4bit-qlora, group-size=128, per-channel. Command I used:
```bash
rdw-eval run --dataset quickpack_v2 --model restream-cust-lora:v3-merge-2026-03-19 --quant int4-qlora --batch 8 --metrics turn_coherence,bleu,perplexity
```
Output snip:
```
turn_coherence: 0.758 (baseline 0.785)
bleu: 0.321 (baseline 0.333)
perplexity: 14.8 (baseline 14.0)
```

Vikram: Hm. 3% on turn_coherence is worth digging. Two quick asks: 1) run the same merged LoRA on float16 to confirm loss comes from quant or merging. 2) run a short warm-cache pass (prefix caching) — sometimes int4 + cache scheduling change flips context alignment.

Marta: Will do float16 in a minute. Warm-cache pass what command?

Vikram: same eval with `--cache-warm 200` and `--prefix-cache=true`. Also try `group-size=64` to see kernel selection effect.

Olivia: I can kick off an A/B with the customer's own prompt subset (their top 200 extremes). Good to see customer-specific failure modes.

Jules: CI bot FYI — smoke tests for restream-cust-lora:v3-merge-2026-03-19 completed: unit tests passed, runtime integration: OK, inference sanity: OK. (ci-bot) :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: perf snapshot uploaded: s3://rdw-artifacts/evals/4132100000/restream-bakeoff-snapshot.json

Marta: Float16 run — results quick look: turn_coherence 0.783 (almost baseline). So merge itself probably fine; quant path is suspect.

Vikram: Good call. Try `--quant int4-qlora --quant-backend=per-channel-symmetric` vs current asymmetric. Also check KV-cache alignment when using 4-bit kernels (we have a known off-by-one with group-size 128 on Ampere kernels).

Marta: Running both quant-backend variants + group-size=64/128 and warm-cache. Will post numbers.

Olivia: I'll prepare the mini-eval pack for the customer's hard prompts and include a few safety/regression checks. Can we include a tiny human annotation pass after the automated runs? quick 20 examples.

Marta: Yes please — highlight hallucinations. If automated metrics show divergence but human says ok, we can accept int4 for this customer.

Vikram: If int4 still bad, fallback plan: offer them int8 quant variant on Dedicated or set routing policy to use float16 for 10% of requests as shadowing A/B.

Marta: All right — will dump the run artifacts and tag this thread. Thanks. :thumbsup:

(48s later) Marta: Uploads: s3://rdw-artifacts/evals/4132100000/int4-perf-compare.json and s3://rdw-artifacts/evals/4132100000/float16-compare.json

Vikram: Thanks — taking a look now.

Olivia: Kicking off human 20-sample pass, tagging @marta when done.

Jules: Noted for postmortem checklist: add int4 kernel group-size test to our pre-merge smoke matrix.
